name: fuel_economy
description: Use when the user reports high fuel consumption, or you need the car's consumption now and over its recent recorded trips.
instructions: Call read_fuel_economy {} once: it gives the instant consumption from live values (L/100 km while moving, L/h at standstill) and the average L/100 km and distance of this car's last 5 trips.
The stationary car only gives L/h at idle; judge consumption mainly on the trip averages.
Call list_trips {} when you need the trips' durations, max coolant or max rpm to explain a high average.
interpret: The instant figure comes from the engine fuel rate (015E) when the car reports it, else it is estimated from MAF (0110): the MAF estimate can be off by 10-20 %.
Warm idle fuel flow: roughly 0.5-1.0 L/h for a small petrol or diesel engine. Clearly more at a warm idle points to extra load or a running fault.
Short trips (under 5 km) and a cold engine raise the average a lot: compare trips of similar length before calling consumption high.
A trip average far above the others of similar length, with a low max coolant, points to a thermostat stuck open; with high rpm it is the driving style.
